title: The Dogged Dreamer
subtitle: We have taken in many patients who, after giving up their dreams, are now living quite well.

items.text: The Dogged Dreamer
The finished reels are piled up like a mountain.
They reflect Brian's furrowed brow on their surfaces—his struggle and embarrassment laid bare on the mountainside.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This one's no good. It just doesn't carry the weight of what I want to express. The symbolism's totally missing, and the framing's all wrong!
He removes the reel, replacing it with a new one. He watches in hope.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This one too. The props are all over the place. Ms. Winnifred, you really shouldn't have eaten those grapes—they were meant to balance the shot.
Another reel is set aside. He sighs in resignation.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This one's even worse. The composition's been completely ruined, and the props you added seem to symbolize some kind of material desire, which is totally confusing the message of the film! The insinuations are terrible!
Winnifred nods at Brian, offering a polite apology.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: You're very diligent, Mr. Brian. I'm sure Mr. Danny would be pleased with all this.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Of course, I'll give you a glowing review for the work you've done.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I'm not sure I understand ...

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Haha. Once again, you prove that my coins have been well spent. It appears I haven't lost my knack for striking a good deal.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's not just about the money, Ms. Winnifred, at least not for me.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: He stares at Winnifred, who appears indifferent to this declaration.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: After a moment's hesitation, he cannot help but go on.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ms. Winnifred, with all due respect ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: We should reshoot this material. Over the next few days, I'll prepare more reels and plan a new script for you.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I can't lie to you, ma'am. The truth is, the footage we have now is almost totally unusable. It's monotonous and hollow, and even with extensive editing, it won't meet the standards of a truly great documentary.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I'll handle any additional costs. You just need to—
Winnifred cuts him off.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I don't think that'll be necessary, Mr. Brian.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I've seen the shots. They're terrific.
Brian's tone verges on vexation.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You have to be kidding, right? Look, we'll watch them again, and I'll explain the major flaws to you. Then you'll see for yourself, I swear!

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: You're an outstanding cinematographer, Mr. Brian. You don't need to prove that to me anymore.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Then why won't you agree to my proposal?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: To be honest, I don't really care about the quality of the documentary. All I need is for it to be made and become a shiny new addition to my display case.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Don't you care about its artistic value at all?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Absolutely not. But being in vogue? That's what really matters. You have to understand that women of a certain social class are only interested in the new, and trends can change at the drop of a hat.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: If we don't hurry up and finish shooting this thing, I'll be left in the dust by that prestigious circle chock-full of treasures and opportunities. That's what I'm really afraid of.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Could you imagine me, a has-been, an outcast of the new age, bankrupt without a penny to my name? I've seen that story play out more times than I care to recall.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: She shakes her head dramatically, as if the very notion chills her to the core.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I understand, Ms. Winnifred. Let's get on with the shoot.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Brian shakes his head. He lets out a long sigh but says no more.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Time to shoot the small talk segment. Ms. Winnifred, I'm not sure I'm the right person for this kind of chat ...

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: No, no, it's fine! We can make do with what we have. Now, let's get started!

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Just relax and talk about whatever interests you.
She leans back, settling into a comfortable position on the sofa.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: A-Alright.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Forgive my nosiness, but have you really never believed in the existence of vampires?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I've been around, Brian—seen a lot of places and met many people, but I've never once laid eyes on even half of what you'd call a "vampire."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Of course, plenty of people have tried to buy such secrets from me. And believe me, were there any credence to these rumors, I'd be working to profit from them myself.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: She shakes her head in resignation.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But how, then, do you explain your appearance?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Time seems to have no effect on you whatsoever. If that's not because of some special bloodline, then what else could possibly explain it?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Money.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Sometimes the answer's far simpler than you think, Mr. Brian. Money is a potent magic.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It grants everyone who possesses it a longer life, a healthier body, and a more radiant appearance.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Regardless of the era.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Naturally, I'm a beneficiary of its largesse and shall continue to be so.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Well, you're not wrong about that.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: B-But ...
He closes his notebook.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I must say, I never imagined your answer would be so pragmatic yet so profoundly cruel!
Winnifred nods, fully understanding his frustration.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: The truth will never satisfy everyone, but that's the reality of the situation. Trust me, I'm truly sorry for you, Brian.
Brian's disappointment deepens.
He rises to his feet.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ms. Winnifred! I'm afraid I'll have to withdraw my invitation. You're not fit to play the role of the vampire in my film!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You're nothing like her. Not at all. You're the true vampire of our world—a dyed-in-the-wool capitalist!
The final shot is complete.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Rest assured, ma'am. Divine Union Pictures will edit the film and send it to you as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: We won't delay your pursuit of the latest craze for a second longer than necessary.
Brian bows in her direction and departs without looking back.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Goodbye. I wish you all the best, Mr. Brian.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: And so, that was the last time I ever saw Ms. Winnifred.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I couldn't accept her choices, just as she couldn't stomach my stubbornness.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: A huge, irreparable rift stood decisively between us, and I no longer believed she had anything to do with the fantasies of my childhood.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I even started to think that everything I once firmly believed in was laughable. Absurd, even.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: After that, I threw myself into a career more concerned with reality, and I tried my best to awaken from that unreachable dream.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I couldn't really say whether I succeeded in my ideals or in my career.
TO BE CONTINUED…
